messages:
devsec-bot: ALERT: S3PublicAclDetected for bucket redwood-temp-backups-2026. 23 objects match snapshots/*.tar.gz — public-read ACL.

maria: saw this. tagging triage. i'm going to lock the bucket ACL first. @ajay can you peek at the KMS key used for SSE-KMS on these objects?

ajay: looking now. bucket default encryption = SSE-KMS, kms_key_id = alias/backup/key-2024. key policy has an unexpected statement with Principal = \"*\" in Grants (probably a bad var in terraform). sending snippet.

ajay: ```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowBackupService",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "*"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

leah: ugh. that explains it: objects encrypted but key effectively allowed too-broad access. we need containment: 1) remove public ACLs 2) put an explicit deny bucket policy 3) rotate/create new KMS key and re-encrypt objects 4) search CloudTrail for external access.

maria: applying ACL change now.

maria: run: `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-temp-backups-2026 --acl private`

maria: done — AWS responded 200. bucket-level ACL set to private. listing public objects to confirm.

maria: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-temp-backups-2026 --prefix snapshots/ --query 'Contents[].Key'`

ken: good call. i pushed an immediate bucket policy deny to block any PutBucketAcl/PutObjectAcl public grants and block GetObject to anonymous. policy:

ken: ```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {"Sid":"DenyPublicAcls","Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":["s3:PutBucketAcl","s3:PutObjectAcl"],"Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::redwood-temp-backups-2026/*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"s3:x-amz-acl":"public-read"}}},
    {"Sid":"DenyAnonymousGet","Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:GetObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::redwood-temp-backups-2026/*","Condition":{"Bool":{"aws:ViaAWSService":"false"}}}
  ]
}
```

ajay: removing the wildcard grant from KMS now. creating a strict key policy where only the backup-service role and the infra admins have decrypt.

ajay: steps: 1) create new key alias/backup/key-2026 2) update bucket default encryption to new key 3) run S3 Batch Ops job to re-encrypt objects (copy -> same key) 4) disable old key (after re-encrypt and verifying).

leah: we should also rotate creds for the external backup-service role and audit all principals that used the key. running CloudTrail query for "Decrypt" on alias/backup/key-2024 since 2026-02-01.

maria: initial CloudTrail shows two distinct external IPs performing GetObject on a handful of snapshots between 03:12-03:48 UTC. i exported the event ids to S3 bucket redwood-sec-logs/temp/179999.

natalie: heads-up — sharing with legal and cs now. customer-facing comms draft in /docs/incidents/drafts.legal-review required before notify.

ken: creating incident tracker INC-2026-045 and adding remediation checklist. assigning tasks:
- maria: validate no remaining public objects, generate S3 Inventory report (due +2h)
- ajay: provision new KMS key + BatchOps (due +4h)
- leah: CloudTrail/Access log analysis + IOCs (due +6h)
- ken: patch terraform modules to ensure block_public_acls var defaults to true and add lint rule (PR assigned)
- natalie: legal + customer comms (sensitive)

maria: S3 Inventory kicked off. found 0 objects with public ACLs now. confirming via HEADs for top 20 keys.

ajay: new key created alias/backup/key-2026. default encryption switched. starting S3 Batch Ops job JOB-179999-1 to re-encrypt ~23 objects.

leah: CloudTrail full run in progress. preliminary: no PutObject from unknown principals in the bucket; accesses were GetObject only. need to check if any cross-account grants existed on object ACLs before removal.

maria: quick note: objects were snapshots taken by a temp backup worker role `arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/backup-worker`. terraform var for that account was empty in the module that sets KMS grant -> caused wildcard.

ken: remediation checklist addition: add CI test rejecting any KMS key policy with Principal = "*" and ensure terraform module requires explicit account var.

natalie: legal asked for exact list of affected objects + whether any PII present. maria please flag any objects with logs/traces.

maria: scanning object metadata now for filenames with "user-" or "audit". will flag if found.

ajay: once BatchOps finishes, plan to schedule a controlled disable of old key alias/backup/key-2024 to ensure no lingering decrypt usage. do not schedule before we have re-encrypt and verification.

leah: post-incident actions: 1) account-level S3 Block Public Access ON (if not already) 2) mandatory terraform module update + rolling reapply across accounts 3) new CloudWatch alarm on PutBucketAcl/PublicAcl detection 4) tabletop scheduled with infra + sec + legal.

ken: PR for terraform change and CI tests opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3482 (assigning reviewers).

maria: BatchOps completed. objects re-encrypted with key-2026. Verified decryption using a test GetObject with backup-worker role (allowed) and anonymous requests blocked (403).

leah: searching for data exfil signs — still no evidence of mass download beyond those few GetObject events. preserving logs and exporting to secure bucket for forensics.

natalie: legal ok to prepare a short customer notification template if required; holding until we finish complete scope. will coordinate with ops.

maria: closing containment phase. moving to recovery and postmortem steps. creating postmortem doc draft assigned to @leah (due EOD +2 days).

ken: great work team. follow-ups documented in INC-2026-045. we should avoid repeating the wildcard var mistake — it's a low-effort, high-impact failure mode.

devsec-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2026-045 moved to status: contained -> recovery. Next review meeting scheduled 2026-04-02 15:00 UTC.
